neighboring_unit_entries.title: Pole behavior under elliptic-curve addition
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Lemma 1 shows that adding two points with negative x-valuations preserves a pole and controls its valuation, while adding a pole point to a non-pole point yields a non-pole; the proof uses the sharp ultrametric rule, the addition formula, and decompositions such as P=(P+Q)-Q.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Nonzero constant discriminant forces local equalities
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: After deriving valuation inequalities from coordinate identities and the addition law, the proof represents the curve discriminant as a polynomial combination of the two partial derivatives. Because that nonzero discriminant lies in the constant field and has valuation zero, the possible strict inequalities would force a contradiction, upgrading the local estimates to the equalities in Lemma 2(a).
